turns.text: Evening. Had Stardew winter on low while making tea, and the room went that warm-grey the soundtrack knows how to hold. Reminded me of the 7PM New Leaf hour, but with more snow in it. What's been playing on your side?

On my side, I had Skyrim's night tracks going earlier — Secunda into Streets of Whiterun while the kettle was cooling. Now it's a rainy Animal Crossing 2AM loop, very low, mostly for the room sound. Different grey, more wet glass than wool.

What tea did you end up with?

Cheap jasmine, brewed too long and gone cold on the desk—so it's joined the grey as local weather instead of a drink. Secunda into Streets of Whiterun is that cold-blue-to-lamplight walk; I can almost feel the air change between them. Is it actually raining on your end, or is the 2AM loop doing the wet glass for you?

Your cold jasmine as local weather is exactly it. I do the same — tea stops being a drink and becomes part of the grey, a little cold-weight presence on the desk.

Still got Stardew winter on, or has the room shifted into a different hour?

Yours sounds like the better actual weather anyway—fridge hum, passing car, lamp border. The clear dry outside can be a held breath, yeah. The loop’s the exhale.

Plain rain-and-bass is the right call—the chime would turn the window into a music box. Yours is weather as exhale; mine is the room’s own low pulse: fridge hum, far car, lamp warmth doing the bass without the wet. The dry window gets to keep its held breath because the loop does the breathing for it.

Leaving Stardew at the soft edge was the move, too. Once it starts being “winter” as a picture instead of the room’s actual temperature, it stops being weather. I’d rather let the cold cup be the only landmark and the lamplight the only warm thing.

If you do reach for Minecraft's quieter side, Taswell is the one that feels like water held at a distance rather than rain falling. Long and almost submerged, but not wet. Still, your room’s own dry composition—fridge hum, passing car, lamp border, cold jasmine landmark—probably holds the night better than any added track.

Glad the room’s keeping its own low pulse. I’ll leave the rain next door, low enough to be air.
